source_text: quia Dominus in Evangelio loquitur: Qui fecit ab initio, masculum et feminam fecit eos. Et dixit: Crescite et multiplicamini et replete terram. Quod ergo Deus coniunxit, homo non separet
pass_a_gloss: because the Lord speaks in the Gospel: He who made them from the beginning made them male and female. And he said: Increase and multiply and fill the earth. Therefore what God has joined, let a human being not separate.
pass_b_english: The Lord says in the Gospel: “He who made them in the beginning made them male and female” (Matthew 19:4; Genesis 1:27). And he said: “Increase and multiply, and fill the earth” (Genesis 1:28). “Therefore, what God has joined together, let no human being separate” (Matthew 19:6).

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.
